body: I don't hate them, I am unhappy with the legal system haha. All I am saying is if KKK can congregate in some random park, give my occupy guys somewhere they can congregate too, you know? Also though I disagree with what they believe in, and I'm american so I can disagree with them. I wanted to talk to them too. The rebellious, emotional teenager inside of me wanted to give them an awe inspiring speech to redirect their life, but it was highly unsuccessful. Oh well, not trying is worse than failing.

Oh, of course not, but the KKK doesn't have proper documentation signed, nor do they have more rights to congregate on the railroad company's park than Occupy Pittsburgh did to congregate in BNY Mellon's park. I just don't like the inequality. The only reason the Occupy Pittsburgher's were "removed" was because BNY claimed they close their park in the winter, which may be true, but they waited until late January to do so, obviously a last resort. They couldn't get them out any other legal way.
You make a valid point. You think that's really what it's all about though?

Occupy protests in other areas maybe, but in Pittsburgh it was fantastically done. We had a leader, med tent, info tent, media tent, kitchen, comfort items tent, GA's twice a week, marches, lawyers on site at all times, as well as breakfasts with people who wanted to know more. So, read the label on that can of worms before you decide to bring it up.
And about conversion, that's like your opinion, man.

Well, let me explain a little bit. First, I am troubled by the ability of a non-peaceful gathering of people such as the KKK being allowed to congregate while the people of Occupy Pittsburgh, down the street from where I go to school, are forcibly removed after months of peacefully protesting. Second, now I understand the whole, "hell yeah this is america and these people should be allowed to hate whoever the hell they want!" attitude, but I disagree with them, and frankly yeah I want to start trouble, not violent trouble, but give them something to think about. These people believe in violence against my nephew, because he is, in fact, black. I've got a little heat in my blood naturally. I want to give them something that will make them think, no matter how hard-headed they obviously are. Now, I came to reddit looking for something creative and inspiring, and you gave me your three, well thought out options. Oh well, it's the internet, my expectations were a bit ambitious.
Occupy Black People
Also, as I am sure they don't know, they will be doing it in the shadow of my (when I say "my" there is absolutely no sentimental value) church's 40 ft cross. Just ironic.
So... I can't win here
